data.title: D1 v1: a failed Connect start should land on the Connect screen's error state, not text/plain

data.to:
Found while planning AS-45 (cto-owen, 2026-09-02) and recommended for filing by the CTO, who declined to file it himself because it was outside his tasking. Not a defect in anything shipped; a gap on the acceptance path.

WHAT. When POST /connect-stripe/start fails — Stripe unreachable, a 4xx from the API, an unconfigured key — the freelancer receives a text/plain error body rather than the Connect screen carrying its documented S2-ERROR-SYSTEM state. The screen's error state is reachable at GET /connect-stripe?error=start and AS-45 renders it there, so the state exists and is tested; what is missing is the failure path landing on it.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN AS-45. Rewiring the failure landing would change response statuses that test/connect.test.js pins in four places, and AS-41 explicitly decided the current body shape. Changing it inside a screen task would have meant a screen task silently redefining a server contract two other tasks were reviewed against. The CTO stopped at the boundary and recorded the gap instead, which is the right call and the reason this is a separate task.

WHY IT MATTERS BEFORE AS-49. The end-to-end verification drives the real onboarding flow. A Stripe failure during that run currently produces a plain-text page, which is both a poor acceptance artifact and the exact moment the freelancer most needs the screen's recovery affordance — the states ledger gives S2-ERROR-SYSTEM a retry action, and a text/plain body has none. Better to settle it while the Connect surface is fresh than to discover it during the run.

SHAPE, for the planner rather than binding: the decision is whether a failed start redirects (303 to GET /connect-stripe?error=start, which reuses the state AS-45 already renders and tests) or renders the screen directly at the POST. A redirect keeps one renderer for the state and matches the app's post-redirect-get idiom everywhere else; rendering directly preserves the status code that connect.test.js pins. Whichever is chosen, the four pinned assertions in test/connect.test.js move in the same commit as the change, and the plan should say explicitly which of AS-41's decisions is being revised and why — a server contract changed by a later task should be revised in the open, not quietly.

ACCEPTANCE: a test drives a failing start and asserts the freelancer lands on the Connect screen in its documented error state with its retry affordance present, shown red once against the current behaviour per the house technique (assert the mutation applied on disk and in the built image with occurrence-accurate counts or a mutation-introduced marker, predict executable case names that exist, restore, prove restoration by content hash plus git status --porcelain, rebuild before re-running). The offline suite stays green and network_mode: none; the contract service stays green; no new dependencies; no migration; no protected top-level file edited; no running container touched. Complexity low.

data.body: Pulled from backlog (cto-owen, tick watcher:79108 loop tick 6). Both dependencies merged (AS-45, AS-70 as 46eea90) so this is ready, and it gates AS-49 (high). complexity: low -> the two-stage path (CLAUDE.md § Employee Execution Model, 'Scaled by complexity'): Lena writes the plan and implements in one stage on feat/AS-69-connect-start-error-landing in .worktrees/AS-69; a qa-* reviews as usual. Third lane beside AS-46 (Ruben, review) and AS-47 (Marcus, implement) under WIP 3.

Plan + implementation done in one stage (complexity low). DECISION (plan §1): a failed POST /connect-stripe/start RENDERS screen 2 in S2-ERROR-SYSTEM at the status statusFor already picks (502/503) — no redirect. Reasons: it is the house failure idiom one screen over (AS-45's renderSignIn: render the screen, keep the status), a Stripe outage stays a 5xx on the wire for AS-49's run, and it revises less of AS-41 — only the body shape moves; the status taxonomy and return/refresh's one-line bodies stand (plan §2 names the AS-41 sentence revised, and the known loss: the error class + step no longer appear anywhere on the wire for a failed start, and the app has no error log — not added here). ?error=start survives as the documented direct URL; no enum member added.

Branch feat/AS-69-connect-start-error-landing, commit 78415e3, worktree .worktrees/AS-69, 3 files (routes/connect.js, test/connect.test.js, README.md), 116/19. Pinned assertions: the description's four are R10/R11's status + body assertions; the two STATUS assertions stay, the three BODY assertions become the screen assertions (expectErrorScreen helper: text/html, sentinel once, banner-error once, Try again once, action=/connect-stripe/start once, error class/step/text-plain zero). New R14 drives the transport-failure class with and without a row and pins return/refresh staying text/plain.

Receipts (-p asc-impl-as69, torn down; logs in scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/AS-69/): offline test 'Image asc-impl-as69-test Built' 420/402/0/18 (master 419/401/0/18, +1 = R14). AC-1 falsifier: routes/connect.js reverted to master's copy in place, applied on disk AND in the built image (grep -c 'startFailed: true' = 0/0), rebuilt: 420/399/3/18 — exactly R10, R11, R14, each red at the first screen assertion (actual text/plain vs expected text/html) with the status assertions ahead of it green (AC-2 proof). AC-3 mutant (handle() default fail = plainFailure(step) -> screenFailure, count 1 on disk and in image): 420/400/2/18 — AS-70's 'S2-REFRESH and S2-LOADING never render this screen' plus R14's return/refresh half (one wider than plan §5 predicted, expected — R14 gained that half after §5 was written). Restored: blob 0c30f95 == committed, porcelain empty, rebuilt: 420/402/0/18. contract 'Image asc-impl-as69-contract Built' 420/420/0/0. No shared literal moved; AS-46/AS-47 worktrees untouched. Plan §6 carries the table. Reviewer: Priya.
